categories.title: Quality Control
categories.description: Assess read quality, trim adapters, and filter low-quality sequences before assembly.
categories.intro: Generally speaking, quality control (QC) is a technique most commonly applied to raw read data. This ensures that the data going into the assembly (the common next step) is of high quality. Poor read quality can result in mis- or incorrectly assembled sequences. Most frequently, read data QC involves trimming reads according to their quality scores and removing barcoding sequences (if applicable). Although some assemblers do not require QC'd reads, we highly recommend it!

categories.title: Assembly
categories.description: Assemble short reads into contigs for downstream viral identification and analysis.
categories.intro: Once reads have passed quality control and are 'cleaned', the next usual step is to assemble them. Since reads are fragments of a longer DNA template, assembly attempts to piece back together the original DNA sequence from the short reads. This process results in what are commonly called 'contigs' — or contiguous sequences — that represent a larger piece of DNA from the original library. Multiple assemblers are available, each with different methods and algorithms. The choice of assembler can also depend on the complexity of the sample as well as the type of organism. For viruses, SPAdes or MetaSPAdes have yielded good results.

categories.title: Viral Identification
categories.description: Detect viral sequences from metagenomic assemblies using diverse detection strategies.
categories.intro: Identifying viral sequences from metagenomic assemblies remains a major challenge in the field of viral ecology. A variety of approaches have been proposed, each dependent on the source of data and the underlying biological question. Tools range from signal-based approaches that look for hallmark viral genes to machine learning models trained on sequence composition. We recommend running multiple identification tools and using CheckV to assess the quality and completeness of predicted viral genomes before proceeding to annotation.

categories.title: Gene Calling
categories.description: Predict protein-coding genes from viral contigs prior to annotation and database search.
categories.intro: Post assembly, gene prediction is the next step. Genes determined from a gene prediction tool can be fed into numerous sequence analysis tools, including annotation pipelines, sequence search tools, and taxonomic classifiers. For metagenomic data, anonymous mode (no genome-specific training) is recommended.

categories.title: Annotation
categories.description: Annotate viral genomes, characterize functions, and curate sequences for downstream ecology.
categories.intro: Viral genome annotation assigns putative functions to predicted genes by comparing them against curated reference databases. Beyond basic gene labeling, annotation tools like DRAM-v specifically identify auxiliary metabolic genes (AMGs) — viral genes co-opted from host metabolism that can influence biogeochemical cycles. Annotation results are also used to manually screen viral contigs for false positives and to prepare sequences for database submission.

categories.title: Sequence Search
categories.description: Search nucleotide or protein sequences against reference databases at scale.
categories.intro: Once genes are called — and sometimes that step isn't required — the real fun of analyzing viral sequence data begins. The tools featured here aren't virus-specific, but they're routinely used with viral data to compare predicted proteins against large reference databases at high speed.

categories.title: Taxonomy
categories.description: Assign taxonomic labels to viral sequences using gene-sharing networks or k-mer similarity.
categories.intro: Taxonomic classification of uncultivated viruses is challenging because most lack close relatives in reference databases. A relatively recent and powerful approach organizes viral sequence space through gene-sharing networks: viruses that share a significant fraction of their protein content are grouped into genus-level clusters benchmarked against ICTV-classified reference genomes. Viruses co-clustering with classified references inherit their taxonomy; isolated clusters represent putative novel genera. For species-level demarcation, nucleotide-similarity tools like VIRIDIC complement the protein-based network approach.

categories.title: Host Prediction
categories.description: Predict the prokaryotic hosts of viral sequences using sequence- or signal-based methods.
categories.intro: Predicting the prokaryotic hosts of environmental viruses is essential for understanding their ecological roles, yet most viruses lack cultivated hosts. Host prediction tools exploit signals such as CRISPR spacer matches, sequence composition similarity, and co-occurrence patterns to infer the likely host genus. No single method is perfect, so integrated approaches that combine multiple signals — such as iPHoP — generally outperform single-method tools.

categories.title: Abundance & Ecology
categories.description: Map reads back to viral references to estimate genome abundance and population dynamics.
categories.intro: Read-based analyses can be used for a variety of reasons, but chief among them is estimating genome or population abundance. By mapping raw reads back to a set of reference viral genomes, these tools calculate coverage depth and breadth across samples — enabling comparisons of viral community structure, population dynamics, and ecological patterns across environments or time points.

categories.title: Visualization
categories.description: Explore and visualize viral networks, community structure, and genomic context.
categories.intro: Visualization tools help make sense of complex viral datasets by rendering gene-sharing networks, genome arrangements, and community structure in interactive or publication-quality graphics. Network-based tools like Cytoscape are commonly used to explore vConTACT2 output, while platforms like Anvi'o provide a unified environment for inspecting read coverage, pangenomics, and genome annotations in a single interactive browser.

items.name: fastp
items.summary: All-in-one FASTQ preprocessor for quality control and adapter trimming. Faster and more feature-rich than older tools like Trimmomatic.

items.name: FastQC
items.summary: Generates per-sample quality reports for raw sequencing reads. Commonly paired with MultiQC for batch summaries.

items.name: Trimmomatic
items.summary: Flexible trimmer for Illumina reads; removes adapters and low-quality bases using a sliding-window approach.

items.name: MetaSPAdes
items.summary: Extension of SPAdes designed specifically for metagenomic datasets with uneven coverage — the recommended assembler for most viral metagenomes.

items.name: SPAdes
items.summary: Trusted assembler for short-read microbial and viral datasets with even coverage.
items.reference: Bankevich et al., J Comput Biol (2012)

items.name: MEGAHIT
items.summary: Ultra-fast, memory-efficient assembler suited for large and highly complex metagenomes.

items.name: IDBA-UD
items.summary: De novo assembler handling uneven sequencing depth — useful for single-cell and metagenomic data.

items.name: VirSorter2
items.summary: Multi-classifier, expert-guided approach for detecting diverse DNA and RNA viruses — the current recommended successor to VirSorter.

items.name: VIBRANT
items.summary: Automated recovery, annotation, and curation of viral genomes from metagenomes using protein profiles and machine learning.

items.name: DeepVirFinder
items.summary: Identifies viral sequences in metagenomes using a deep learning model trained on sequence composition — works without requiring gene predictions.

items.name: MARVEL
items.summary: Predicts bacteriophage sequences within metagenomic bins using random forest classification on genomic features.

items.name: VirSorter
items.summary: Original signal-based tool for mining viral signatures from microbial genomic data. Superseded by VirSorter2 for most use cases.

items.name: Prodigal
items.summary: Fast, accurate prokaryotic gene prediction — the standard gene caller used upstream of most viral annotation and search pipelines.

items.name: Prokka
items.summary: Rapid whole-genome annotation pipeline for prokaryotic genomes, including phage and viral sequences, producing GenBank-ready output.

items.name: DRAM-v
items.summary: Distills viral genome annotation into structured metabolic profiles, identifying auxiliary metabolic genes (AMGs) and their ecological relevance.
items.reference: Shaffer et al., Nucleic Acids Res (2020)

items.name: Cenote-Taker 2
items.summary: Automates virus discovery and sequence annotation by detecting hallmark genes, curating genomes, and preparing sequences for GenBank submission.

items.name: VIGA
items.summary: Viral genome annotation pipeline for prokaryotic viruses; produces GenBank-compatible output from assembled contigs.

items.name: DIAMOND
items.summary: Ultra-fast protein and translated DNA alignment against large reference databases — up to 100× faster than BLAST with comparable sensitivity.

items.name: vConTACT2
items.summary: Assigns taxonomy to uncultivated prokaryotic viruses using gene-sharing networks benchmarked against the ICTV classification — the community standard for phage taxonomy.
items.reference: Bin Jang et al., Nat Biotechnol (2019)

items.name: vConTACT2-Gene2Genome
items.summary: Preprocessing step for vConTACT2 — converts protein FASTA sequences into the gene-to-genome mapping file required by the classifier.
items.reference: Bin Jang et al., Nat Biotechnol (2019)

items.name: CAT/BAT
items.summary: Taxonomic classification of assembled contigs (CAT) and metagenome-assembled bins (BAT) using diamond-based alignment and a last common ancestor approach.
items.reference: von Meijenfeldt et al., Genome Biol (2019)

items.name: WIsH
items.summary: Predicts prokaryotic hosts of viruses from metagenomic data using a homogeneous Markov chain model trained on genome composition.

items.name: HostPhinder
items.summary: Predicts phage host range based on k-mer similarity between phage and host genomes.

items.name: Read2RefMapper
items.summary: Maps short reads to a reference set of viral genomes to estimate relative genome abundance across samples.

items.name: BowtieBatch
items.summary: Batch wrapper around Bowtie2 for mapping multiple read datasets to a shared viral reference in parallel.

items.name: Cytoscape
items.summary: Network visualization and analysis platform widely used to explore and render gene-sharing networks generated by vConTACT2.

items.name: Anvi'o
items.summary: Advanced multi-omics analysis and visualization platform — used for pangenomics, metagenome-assembled genome inspection, and viral community profiling.

items.name: MultiQC
items.summary: Aggregates QC results from FastQC, Trimmomatic, fastp, and dozens of other tools into a single interactive HTML report — essential for batch sample assessment.

items.name: BBDuk / BBTools
items.summary: Versatile read trimming and filtering toolkit from the JGI. BBDuk handles adapter removal, quality trimming, contaminant filtering, and length filtering in one or two fast passes.

items.name: CheckV
items.summary: Assesses quality and completeness of metagenome-assembled viral genomes, removes host contamination from integrated proviruses, and classifies sequences as complete, high-, medium-, or low-quality draft.

items.name: PropagAtE
items.summary: Estimates whether an integrated prophage is in lytic (actively replicating) or lysogenic (dormant) state by comparing read coverage of the prophage region to that of the host chromosome.

items.name: VIRIDIC
items.summary: Calculates intergenomic similarity between phage genomes using BLAST-based nucleotide comparisons, enabling genus- and species-level demarcation following ICTV criteria.

items.name: iPHoP
items.summary: Integrated machine learning framework that combines multiple host-prediction signals (CRISPR spacers, k-mer similarity, gene-sharing) for high-accuracy host genus prediction of archaeal and bacterial viruses.

items.name: PhageTerm
items.summary: Determines phage genome termini and packaging mechanisms (cos sites, pac sites, DTR/ITR) from sequencing read depth at genome ends — useful for correctly circularizing and orienting phage assemblies.
